Looking at the code in `lib/index.js`:

1. When processing defaults (lines 44-49):
```javascript
if (defaults) {
    for (k in opts.default) {
        opts.alias[k] = opts.alias[k] || [];
        (opts[typeof opts.default[k]] || []).push(k);  // THIS IS THE PROBLEM
    }
}
```

This code pushes default keys into `opts.boolean` or `opts.string` based on the default value's type. So when `{ bar: false }` is the default, `'bar'` gets pushed into `opts.boolean`.

```javascript
: !!~opts.boolean.indexOf(key) ? (val === 'false' ? false : val === 'true' || (out._.push((x = +val,x * 0 === 0) ? x : val),!!val))
```

When the key is found in `opts.boolean`, it evaluates this complex expression. The problem is the expression `val === 'true' || (out._.push(...), !!val)`. If `val` is the boolean `true` (not the string `'true'`), the comparison `val === 'true'` is `false`, so it falls through to the `out._.push(...)` part, pushing `1` into the array.

The fix is to remove the line that adds default keys to `opts.boolean`/`opts.string` since it's not needed - defaults are applied later in the code and shouldn't affect the type coercion during parsing.
